summary: Verified charge.refunded partial vs full handling in routes.payments._process_stripe_event + regression for checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.expired, payment_intent.succeeded, and POST /api/webhooks/stripe unverifiable->400. All 7 iter34 tests PASS and all 10 iter33 regression tests PASS. Charge.refunded now correctly sets 'partially_refunded' when refunded=False (refund_amount=45.0 for 4500 cents on $60 booking) and 'refunded' when refunded=True (refund_amount=60.0 for 6000 cents).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/payments.py _process_stripe_event charge.refunded branch now correctly distinguishes partial vs full refunds using charge.refunded bool. Looks good.
payments.py is 1068 lines — consider splitting into stripe/paypal/card_hold submodules for maintainability (not blocking).

In _process_stripe_event the charge.refunded branch only updates the specific tx matched by stripe_payment_intent; if a booking has multiple txs for the same PI (e.g., partial refund then another partial), only the first-matched tx is updated. Current flow is single-tx-per-PI so OK, but worth noting.

rca of the issue: Previous bug: charge.refunded branch unconditionally set payment_status='refunded' regardless of partial vs full refund. Main-agent fix: refund_state = 'refunded' if charge.get('refunded') else 'partially_refunded'; amt_refunded = charge.amount_refunded/100. Verified: amount_refunded=4500, refunded=False -> partially_refunded, 45.0; amount_refunded=6000, refunded=True -> refunded, 60.0.
